lens: Architecture adherence — ADR-0056 12-layer + clean-architecture inward flow
answer: PR #13 retires the archive-orphan kernel + app pair atomically on dev (merge 59534679). Layer direction (app -> kernel) is preserved through the retirement: the only importer of oya-foundry-fitness-archive-orphan-kernel was tools/oya-foundry-fitness-archive-orphan-app, and both were removed together. A full origin/dev workspace grep ('archive_orphan', 'archive-orphan-kernel', 'fitness-archive-orphan-kernel', 'fitness-archive-orphan-app', 'fitness_archive_orphan') returns zero hits in crates/, tools/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock — no lingering kernel/domain/usecase/app transitively imports the deleted kernel. tools/oya-foundry-pr-review-dispatcher-app/Cargo.toml only changed comment text mentioning archive-orphan retirement; its real dependency graph (oya-foundry-account-kernel, oya-foundry-subagent-runtime-kernel, oya-foundry-subagent-runtime-usecase) is composition-root-correct (app -> usecase -> kernel, inward flow per ADR-0056). ADR-0107 amendment swaps the archive-orphan row from 'RENAME -> *-app' to 'RETIRED by ADR-0118' and keeps the canonical -app suffix rule intact for all other tools/ crates; the implicit-app exception remains REMOVED and the 13-value layer enum binding is untouched. ADR-0118 retirement reasoning is correctly grounded in ADR-0116 + M01-P18 substrate, supersedes ADR-0052, and relates to ADR-0110/0111/0112/0113. Single A4 nit: ADR-0118 does NOT cite ADR-0056 (the 12-layer enum) in its retirement justification, even though the retirement removes a kernel + app pair that lived under that enum. The retirement is architecturally neutral with respect to the enum (no layer added/removed), so this is documentary completeness rather than a layer violation — MINOR.
